Also class here: Men’s Love (ML) manga. Use for: manga or other East Asian style comics focusing on male same-sex love, usually created by gay men for a gay male audience. Use with: 5PSG and 5X as appropriate
Itt kell osztályozni: Hentai, seijin Manga. Felnőttek számára készült termék nyíltan szexuális vagy erőszakos természetű jelenetekkel; használja az 5X módosítóval, ha szükséges See also: XAMX2
Use for: Manga or other East Asian style comics designed for adults (over about 18 years), of an extreme erotic or pornographic nature. Use with: Qualifier 5X as appropriate See also: XAML

Also class here: shoujo-ai, baihe. Use for: Manga or other East Asian style comics featuring young female same-sex relationships often (but not exclusively) for a young female readership. Use with: 5PSL as appropriate
Also class here: post-underground comics, independent comics, indie comics, auteur comics, small press comics, new wave comics, creator-owned comics, art comics, underground comix, etc

Code.CodeDescription: Rajzos / rajzolt regény és képregény: műfajok
Code.CodeNotes: Use all XQ* codes with: F* or YF* codes, as applicable, to give further extra level of details of fiction genres where required, or, for non-fiction, with A*–W* or relevant Y* codes, as applicable, to indicate the key subject of narrative, for example a comic about an action war story use with FJM*, but one where war or conflict is the background, use with FXF

Code.CodeDescription: Rajzos / rajzolt regény és képregény: memoárok, igaz történetek és nem-regényes ábrázolások
Code.CodeNotes: Itt kell osztályozni: bandes dessinées d’auteur’ (francia-belga szerzői munkák)

Code.CodeDescription: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Educational
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: titles published as comics or manga where the content is primarily non-fiction and aimed at educating people about the subject. Use with: YN* codes if for young people or other relevant non-fiction A*– W* codes for titles aimed at adults, and use with relevant XA* code to indicate type. If created for use in educational institutions use with YP* codes and EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE 4* Qualifiers as appropriate, for graphic medicine or other comics about health or medical or public health topics use with VF* codes or YPJJ6 for educational works for schools, or educational titles about science or technology, use with P* or T* codes or YPM* codes

Code.CodeDescription: Rajzos / rajzolt regény és képregény: irodalmi adaptációk, feldolgozások
Code.CodeNotes: Itt kell osztályozni: korábban létező irodalmi művek grafikus vagy rajzos formájú adaptálása

Code.CodeDescription: Rajzos / rajzolt regény: film- és TV-adaptációk
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: stories that were published as spin-offs or companions to pre-existing non-book media or merchandise, for example story books based on a popular film franchise, an online game or a TV series. DO NOT USE: for titles that were subsequently made into films etc

Code.CodeDescription: Rajzos / rajzolt regény és képregény: bűnügyi, krimi, misztériumregények és thrillerek
Code.CodeNotes: Use with: FF* or FH* YFC* codes to give further details of crime or thriller genres where required

Code.CodeDescription: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Society / culture
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: chroniques sociales, contemporary cultural, political or social topics or issues, comics that present aspects of the arts, culture, food, cuisine, music or society either as a story or as a work of non-fiction, etc. Use with: codes from A*– W* for works of non-fiction aimed adults to give more specific details about the topic covered or Y* codes for works aimed at children or teenagers, to give further details where required

Code.CodeDescription: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Idol / celebrity
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Idol manga, Idol manhwa. Use for: comics where the main theme of the story is about idols or celebrities, or the search to become an idol, sometimes linked to famous singers, entertainers or multimedia stars, such as stars of K-pop, as well as fictional idols or groups

Code.CodeDescription: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Modern and contemporary fiction / literature
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: comic books that are works of fiction or original stories, that do not fall into another fiction genre. Use with: F* or YF* codes to give further details of fiction genres where required. Prefer: XQB for novels or other works of literature that were adapted into comics See also: XQB

Code.CodeDescription: Rajzos / rajzolt regény és képregény: akció és kaland
Code.CodeNotes: Use with: FJ* or YF* codes to indicate genre as appropriate, for example for war stories use with FJM* codes, for martial arts stories, use with FJD, or with YFC* codes for comics aimed at children or teenagers

Code.CodeDescription: Rajzos / rajzolt regény és képregény: western
Rajzos / rajzolt regény és képregény: horror
Code.CodeNotes: Use with: FK* or other F* or YFD codes to indicate specific genres, plus VXQ* or YNX* codes as appropriate

Code.CodeDescription: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Sports
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: comic books featuring sports, athletic and competitive pursuits. Use with: FG or YFR for works of fiction and S* or YNW* codes for non-fiction works to give more specific details of which sport as appropriate

Code.CodeDescription: Rajzos / rajzolt regény és képregény: szuperhősök és szupergonoszok
Code.CodeNotes: Use with: other XQ* codes as appropriate

Code.CodeDescription: Rajzos / rajzolt regény és képregény: sci-fi (tudományos-fantasztikus regények
Code.CodeNotes: Use with: FL* or YFG* codes to give further details of science fiction genres where required

Code.CodeDescription: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Science fiction: Mecha and robots
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Super-robots, real robots, transforming robots, armour, machines, AI technology

Code.CodeDescription: Rajzos / rajzolt regény és képregény: fantázia, ezotérikus
Code.CodeNotes: Használja a mitikus, titkos vagy ezotérikus tudás hagyományait hordozó képregényekhez

Code.CodeDescription: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Fantasy: Magical Girl / Magical Boy / Magical Creature
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: maho shojo, majokko. Use for: comics featuring characters with magical abilities

Code.CodeDescription: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Fantasy: Portal fantasy / Isekai / Other worlds
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: travel to parallel universes or other worlds, crossing to other worlds, otherworld‘s, world hopping, alternate realities

Code.CodeDescription: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Anthropomorphic / animal stories
Code.CodeNotes: Use with: other XQ* codes as appropriate

Code.CodeDescription: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Cultural heritage and Traditional stories, myths, legends
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: mythic fiction, retellings. Use for: stories that often have a long and continuous existence through multiple generations, stories that get told and retold, traditional local folktales, tall tales, folklore, folk literature, wisdom tales, cautionary stories, teaching stories, origin tales, or any form of traditional story told or retold, or modern retellings or works inspired by traditional stories, mythology, legends, fairy tales or folklore in comic book or any sequential art form. Use with: FN* or YFJ or YFH codes to indicate specific genres or QR* or YNRU codes for non-fiction works plus PLACE1* qualifiers, to indicate a particular tradition, as appropriate

Code.CodeDescription: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Slice of life
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Iyashikei. Use for: stories that are based on ordinary, everyday life, or parts of a character’s life, or a sequence of events in a characters life or mundane experiences in a characters life

Code.CodeDescription: Rajzos / rajzolt regény és képregény: románc
Code.CodeNotes: Use with: FR* or YFM codes to give further details of romance genres where required

Code.CodeDescription: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: School / college life
Code.CodeNotes: Use with: other XQ* codes or F* or YF* codes to indicate genre plus 5L* code as appropriate

Code.CodeDescription: Rajzos / rajzolt regény és képregény: humoros
Code.CodeNotes: Use with: other XQ* codes as appropriate or WH* codes or YFQ as appropriate

Use with: F* codes for specific genres of historical fiction aimed at adults or YFT for historical fiction aimed at children or teenagers, OR with specific N* codes for adults or YNH* codes for works aimed at children or teenagers that are non-fiction history titles about particular periods or topics in history, and use with PLACE * plus TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers as appropriate

Code.CodeDescription: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Religious, spiritual, inspirational
Code.CodeNotes: Use with: INTEREST 5PG* qualifiers, F* or YF* for specific genres of fiction, or QR*, VX* or YNR* codes for non-fiction titles

Code.CodeDescription: Rajzos / rajzolt regény és képregény: felnőtt (erotikus, extrém erőszak)
Code.CodeNotes: Itt kell osztályozni: nyílt szexuális vagy erőszakos természetű jeleneteket bemutató, felnőttek számára készült képregények; használja az SX módosítóval, ahol szzükséges See also: XAMX

Code.CodeDescription: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Adult – erotic
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: comic books designed for adults featuring scenes of an overtly erotic nature or dealing with graphic sexual themes only suitable for an aware mature audience. Use with: Qualifier 5X plus other X* codes as appropriate See also: XAMX2

Code.CodeDescription: Graphic novel / Comic book / Manga: Adult – extreme violence / gore
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: comic books designed for adults featuring scenes of an overtly violent or gory nature or dealing with graphic or disturbingly violent themes only suitable for an aware mature audience. Use with: Qualifier 5X plus other X* codes as appropriate See also: XAMX

Code.CodeDescription: Rajzos / rajzolt regény és képregény: kalauzok, ismertetések és kritikák
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: History of Comics, comic studies. Use with: other subject codes as appropriate, for example, with FZ for Companion works or DSB* for histories of comic books or GB* codes for reference works, or DS* for works that analyse, study, critique comic books or Graphic narrative studies, AKLC* for works about comic book art or Sequential art studies, or other subject codes for titles about comics See also: DSR FZ

Use with: other subject codes as appropriate, for example, with FZ for Companion works or DSB* for histories of manga or GB* codes for reference works, or DS* for works that analyse, study, critique manga See also: DSR FZ
Itt kell osztályozni: 3–5 panelből álló, jellemzően humoros képsorozat-gyűjteményeket, amelyek eredetileg újságokban vagy magazinokban jelentek meg See also: YNUC

Code.CodeDescription: Gyermekek és serdülőkorúak számára írt könyvek, oktatási célra szánt konyvek
Code.CodeNotes: Use all Y* codes for: material aimed at, or purposefully written or created for a juvenile or adolescent audience (except for graphic novels, comic books, manga in X*). DO NOT USE: code ‘Y’ itself, but select specific categories from section Y*. Use all Y* codes with: only one INTEREST AGE 5A* Qualifier to indicate a guideline starting interest age (detailed age ranges should be included in other metadata) – or for YP* use EDUCATIONAL PURPOSE 4* qualifiers. All other qualifiers can be used as appropriate with Y* codes. DO NOT USE for: material intended primarily for adults that may also appeal to older teenagers. For ‘new adult’ content see note at 5LKE, for ‘Young Adult’ use the most appropriate 5A* Qualifier according to local usage of the term. NB: Y* codes should be used along with X* codes for graphic novels, comic books, manga. Y* codes may be used in combination with A*– W* codes but always prefer Y* codes and if mixing Y* codes with A*– W* codes, the Y* code must ALWAYS be designated as the Main Subject and sent with one 5A* qualifier. If sending A*– W* codes as Main Subject, then Y* codes should NOT be included except for JNU / JNUM with YP* or DSYC for reviews or critiques

Code.CodeDescription: Nagyon kicsi gyerekeknek írt könyvek, gyerekképeskönyvek és aktivitáskönyvek. Foglalkoztatók
Code.CodeNotes: Use all YB* codes for: physical or digital items – the headings relate purely to the content, not the format (Format information is described in other metadata). Use all YB* codes with: only one INTEREST AGE 5A* Qualifier to indicate a guideline starting interest age

Use all YBC* codes for: highly illustrated books (typically colour throughout) for children in which the content (either fiction or non-fiction) is conveyed through the use of words and pictures in combination or through pictures alone. A ‘picture book’ differs from a ‘book with illustrations’, in that the pictures it contains are at least as important as the text (if any) and form an essential component of the book. Use all YBC* codes with: other codes from Y* sections as appropriate, for example, YNB for Picture book biographies, or YPCA21 for picture books that are part of a structured reading scheme
Itt kell osztályozni: kisméretű, karton- vagy rongyanyagú képeskönyvek, amelyben nincs vagy alig van szöveg és nincs benne tanulási tartalom sem
Használja minden, TV- vagy filmkarakterre épülő könyvhöz, és minden olyan könyvhöz, amely elfogadott, képileg ábrázolt, számos könyvben vagy egyéb termékben megjelent szereplőket mutat be
Itt kell osztályozni: erőteljes narratív szöveggel kísért képeskönyveket See also: XA* XQ*

Use for: works that are collections or individual stories to be read out loud or listened to by children at bedtime or works about getting ready for bed, going to sleep and bedtime routines, preparing children for bedtime or works that are purposefully created to help soothe or calm a child down and prepare them for sleep or help them to sleep, or are stories about dreaming or dreams
Itt kell osztályozni: a képzeletre és/vagy játékra, pl. játékeszközökre épülő képeskönyvek, gyakran egy képzeletbeli világ megalkotásával

Use for: children’s storybooks that are primarily text, but still contain plentiful illustrations. Usually of a relatively short length and low complexity, divided into very short chapters, and intended for transitioning readers – those moving on from picture storybooks. Use with: relevant YF* codes to indicate the genre of story, as appropriate, or YN* or YX* categories as secondary codes for stories with specific themes. Prefer: X* codes for stories told in comic book or manga form See also: YBCS XA* XQ*

Code.CodeDescription: Gyermekek számára készült interaktív foglalkoztatók, aktivitáskönyvek és csomagok
Code.CodeNotes: Használja a YBG-t a gyermekfoglalkoztató és interaktív tételekhez, mint pl. a csomagkönyvek, matricakönyvek stb. minden korcsoportnak

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s interactive and activity: drawing, colouring and painting
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: books to colour in, magic painting books, books and painting sets, fingerprinting, rubber stamps, connect the dots, dot to dot, paint-by-numbers, stencil books, doodles, finger painting, learning to draw or paint, books to draw in, etc See also: YNA
Itt kell osztályozni: „mágikus szem” könyvek és az olyanok, amelyeknél a cél a tárgy vagy alak megtalálása a képeken See also: YNVP

Also class here: origami, books of paper dolls to dress, paper models to make or assemble, things to cut out or punch-out, dioramas, paper folding, or other activities for children using paper or card
Használja a YBL* kódokat csak az iskola előtti anyagokhoz
Itt kell osztályozni: ABCs könyvek, első szavak könyvei stb

Code.CodeDescription: Korai évek: versek, rímek és szójátékok
Code.CodeNotes: Itt kell osztályozni: gyerekmondókák és nagyon kicsi gyermekek számára szóló egyszerű versikék, nyelvtörők stb. See also: YDP YFV

Also class here: Pre-handwriting skills, pregraphism or pre-graphics skills and activities, writing readiness skills, activities for learning to hold a pen or pen or pencil control and skills, tracing exercises and activities, tracing different types of lines, patterns and shapes. Use for: works that help children acquire the fundamental skills children need to develop before they are able to write or draw

Code.CodeDescription: Korai évek: méret, formák és minták
Korai évek: idő és az évszakok
Code.CodeNotes: Itt kell osztályozni: óraállás leolvasása, nappal és éjjel, hét napjai, az évszakok stb
Also class here: baby animals
Itt kell osztályozni: a napi élet elemeit nagyon kicsi gyermekek számára; mosás, lefekvés, biligyakorlás stb.

Code.CodeDescription: Early years: potty and toilet training
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: titles that talk about poo, wee and farts. Use for: works that explain bodily functions linked to going to the toilet, as well as titles for teaching children how to use a potty or toilet
Also class here: sounds and noises, touch and feel, tastes and smells, fingers and toes, smiles and laughter, faces, peek-a-boo, hide-and-seek, etc

Code.CodeDescription: Korai évek: emberek, akik segítenek nekünk

Code.CodeNotes: Use with: YXF* codes as appropriate
Also class here: books on ships, planes, trains, trucks, cars, bikes, buses, diggers, tractors, and other moving vehicles for the very young
Az YD* kódokkal adja meg a megfelelő 5A* Olvasói kor/szint módosítót is, ahol lehetséges
Használja első kódnak az összes évkönyvhöz, a második kód fogja jelezni a típust vagy tématerületet, ahol lehetséges

Használja az irodalmi formát jelző másik kóddal, ahol szükséges, pl. az YF* kóddal a regényantológiákhoz, a YDP kóddal a versantológiákhoz. Használja csak magában különböző irodalmi formákat tartalmazó antológiákhoz
See also: YBLB YFV

Code.CodeDescription: Gyermek- és serdülőkorú irodalom és igaz történetek
Code.CodeNotes: A YF* kódokkal MINDIG adja meg a megfelelő SA* olvasó kora /szintje módosítót és az SX-et, ahol szükséges, az idősebb olvasók számára explicit anyag jelzésére; Az YF* kódok használhatók a FÖLDRAJZ és KORSZAK módosítókkal, ahol ezek a szempontok különösen fontosak; használja a releváns YN* kódokkal és előttük a különleges témájú regényekhez, amelyeknél az YF*-ben való jelzés nem elégséges; használja a YDC-vel a regényantológiákhoz; használja a megfelelő YX* kóddal és előtte a különleges társadalmi vagy egyéni kérdésekkel foglalkozó regényekhez; használja az X* kódokat a képregény formátumú regényekhez. See also: XA* XQ*
Itt kell osztályozni: a kb.1960 előtt kiadott gyermek- és kamaszregényeket, ill azokat, amelyeket széles körben „klasszikusnak” tekintenek
Itt kell osztályozni: minden jelenkori nem-műfaji gyerek- és kamaszregényt

Code.CodeDescription: Gyermek- / serdülőkorú irodalom: akció- és kalandregények

Code.CodeNotes: Itt kell osztályozni: olyan fizikai formátumú vagy digitális könyvek, ahol az olvasónak választási lehetősége van, hogy hogyan változtassa meg az elbeszélés narraíváját; használja más YF* kóddal és utána a műfaj jelzésére, ha lehetséges See also: YFZW

Code.CodeDescription: Gyermek- / serdülőkorú irodalom: krimi és misztériumregény
Gyermek- / serdülőkorú irodalom: katonai és háborús regény
Gyermek- / serdülőkorú irodalom: horror és kísértettörténetek, hátborzongató elbeszélések
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: scary stories of the paranormal, gothic ghost stories, contemporary and realistic horror stories. Use for: any story that is written to be scary or to give an age appropriate feeling of fear, including stories that turn out not to be scary, stories that feature ghosts (friendly or scary), monsters (frightening or misunderstood), witches (wicked or misrepresented), creepy settings, characters or beings, haunted houses or is any form of supernatural chilling, spooky or scary story. Use with: YNX* codes for stories about specific supernatural or paranormal beings, such as YNXB3 for ghost stories, or other YF* codes, such as YFQ for funny or comedy ghost or horror stories, YFJM for cautionary tales, YFH* for fantasy scary stories, YFHG for horror stories based on myths, YFHT for Dark fantasy horror stories, YFA for classic ghost or horror stories, etc See also: YNXW

Code.CodeDescription: Gyermek- / serdülőkorú irodalom: spekulatív, disztopikus és utopisztikus regény
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: fiction set in dystopian or utopian societies, alternative history fiction. Use with: YFG or other YF* codes if possible

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Apocalyptic and post-apocalyptic stories
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: end of the world stories, dying earth, collapsing or collapsed civilizations. Use for: stories set in worlds trying to prevent, or experiencing or that have already been affected by an apocalypse event, such as runaway climate change, an impact event, resource depletion, nuclear holocaust, pandemics, end times, zombie apocalypse, cybernetic revolts, technological singularity, invasion from space, dysgenics, etc
Use for: stories for children or teenagers with a superhero character or where the main characters are depicted as superheroes

Use with: YNTT for Time travel, time slip, or time loop sci-fi stories, YNXF for stories about extra-terrestrials or UFOs, YNNZ for stories about space travel, YNTC for stories about AI, Mecha, robots or new technology, etc

Also class here: Galactic empires, interstellar or intergalactic wars. Use for: science fiction stories set in space, in imagined galaxies or universes, or on different planets, often with advanced cultures and sophisticated technology and usually featuring main characters who are children or teenagers

Also class here: dieselpunk, cyberpunk, retrofuturism. Use for: science fiction based on an alternative world where, for example in the case of steampunk, 19th century steam power has emerged as the dominant technology

Code.CodeDescription: Gyermek- / serdülőkorú irodalom: fantázia és mágikus realizmus
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: paranormal fantasy, enchanted journeys, alternative worlds, accidental travel, portal fantasy, Isekai. Use all YFH* codes with: YNX* codes as appropriate, with YNXB* codes for stories featuring the paranormal or particular supernatural beings

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Epic fantasy / heroic fantasy
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: sword and sorcery fantasy, quest fantasy, high fantasy

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Magical realism / Magical fantasy
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Magical girl. Use for: works that incorporates fantastic, magical, mythical or supernatural elements into an otherwise real-world or mundane setting, or works where the magic itself – whether a magical object or a character with magical powers – is the subject of the story, rather than simply a means to an end. Use with: YNXW for stories about witches, wizards or magicians or YNXB* codes for other magical creatures

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Mythic fantasy / Myths and Legends fiction
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Myths or legends from any culture told or retold as fiction or in story form, mythological fiction, Arthurian fantasy, Classical fantasy (based on Greek and Roman myths), Shenmo (Gods and Demons), etc. Use for: fiction that is inspired by, or a retelling of, or that in some way draws from the characters, stories or themes of myth, legend, for example, a story based on a popular myth or character from a classic work in a modern setting or a story based on a minor character’s perspective, or that takes a ‘what if’ approach or create a mashup of different genres, for example, legendary character or hero meets dystopian future, or mythology crossed with contemporary adventure story. Use with: PLACE 1*, LANGUAGE 2*, INTEREST 5* Qualifiers to indicate if the story is taken from a particular tradition See also: YNRU YFJ

Also class here: Medieval, Dark Age, Arabian, Celtic, Gunpowder, Prehistoric, Wuxia fantasy. Use for: fantasy that incorporates fantastic elements, such as magic or supernatural beings, into recognisable historic settings, periods, cultures etc. Use with: PLACE 1* and/or TIME PERIOD 3* Qualifiers to indicate setting as appropriate
Itt kell osztályozni: „sötét románc”, vámpírrománc stb.; ahol szükséges
Use for: fantasy stories with darker and frightening themes, often incorporating elements of horror or that have a gloomy and threatening atmosphere or a sense of horror and dread

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Contemporary and urban fantasy
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: fantasy set in the present day or recognisably contemporary settings (according to the time period of its creator)
Itt kell osztályozni: tündérmesék, népmesék, mitoszok és legendák regényes formában See also: YFHG

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction and stories: Folk and Fairy tales
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Fairy tale retellings, fractured fairy tales. Use for: folk and fairy tales from any culture told in a story form, or retellings of these stories, stories inspired by fairy tales

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction and stories: Trickster tales
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: stories that feature a trickster character such as a spirit, a deity, a human or an animal

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction and stories: Creation, founding, origin stories
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: stories about the origins or beginnings of peoples, worlds, places, traditions, etc

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction and stories: Teaching stories
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: Cautionary tales, Wisdom tales. Use for: stories that were created for the transmission of wisdom, knowledge, cultural traditions, oral transmission of stories, or stories that warn or caution young people about specific dangers, to teach a lesson or a general moral issue

Also class here: Faith-inspired or inspirational stories. Use for: fiction that promotes a particular religious, spiritual or visionary message or viewpoint. Use with: 5PG* values from INTEREST 5* Qualifiers or YNR* codes, to indicate the religious tradition, as appropriate

Code.CodeDescription: Gyermek- / serdülőkorú irodalom: románc és párkapcsolati történetek
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: stories that deal with all kinds of relationships with others; for stories where interpersonal relationships are the main theme; or explore the relationship of the main characters, stories that explore relationships within groups, relationships between young people. Use with: YX* to give details of kinds of relationships as appropriate, for example, YXH for stories about relationships in peer groups or relationships with adults from a young persons perspective, 5PHG for stories about found or chosen family See also: YXHB
Use for: stories where the main or primary topic or theme of the narrative is the friendship between different child or teenage main characters

Code.CodeDescription: Children’s / Teenage fiction: Romance and love stories
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: contemporary romance, romantic comedy, romantic drama, stories of first or young love, teenage romances, teenage love-triangles, lost love, unrequited love, high school romance, etc. Use for: stories that are clearly of the romance genre and feature a romantic relationship as the core theme, that are specifically written for teenagers and deal with romance or love stories from a teenage point of view. Use all 5A* age codes for: defining the Y* or X* codes – 5A* age numbers are used instead of named codes, such as juvenile, middle grade, young adult, as these have different meanings in different countries or languages. Select one 5A* code indicating a general guideline starting or base interest age of the content in any works aimed primarily at children or teenagers. All Y* codes (except YP* which use 4* codes) MUST be accompanied by one 5A* qualifier code to give guidance of interest age, for example: book content for an audience of 9 to 12 age group, should use 5AK, as the lower age; content of interest to teenagers should use 5AP or 5AQ; content for older teenagers and young adults should use 5AS, 5AT or 5AU as appropriate. 5AR, 5AX and 5AZ can be used with any relevant subject code. All 5A* codes can be used with X* subject codes if the Comic book is aimed at children or teenagers. DO NOT USE: 5A itself – always use 5A* codes. NB: Greater detail of age range, reading age, interest age etc would be communicated in other metadata

Also class here: High-low readers, Hi-Lo content aimed at children or teenagers. Use for: books that are specially written for or considered suitable for young people who do not want to read, have difficulty reading, or are struggling to read. Usually these books will have a higher interest age and a lower reading age. Content is usually aimed at a particular interest age but the language used is purposefully slightly simpler than most average content aimed at the same interest age in that language, so that it is easier to read or listen to than other titles. These are often titles in specific named collections and will often have notions of levels of difficulty associated with them by the publisher and / or may be accompanied by indications of complexity. Use with: one other 5A* Interest age qualifier. Prefer: 5AX for reluctant adult readers or 5AZ for accessible content and 4L codes for second language titles See also: 5AX 5AZ 4L*

Code.CodeDescription: Interest age: from c 17 years to c 29 years
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works aimed specifically at older teens and young adults in their 20s, those who are newly adult, emerging adulthood. This age group may be referred to in some places as young adults or sometimes as new adults. The content is specifically created for and about this group but can also appeal to other groups as well. Prefer: 5LKE for titles about this age group. DO NOT USE: with Y* codes See also: 5LKE

Also class here: High-low readers, Hi-Lo content aimed at adults. Use for: books that are specifically aimed at adult literacy or helping adult readers with reading difficulties or books that are suitable for adult readers who are not confident in their reading abilities or suitable for the newly literate. Content is aimed at adult interests but the language used is purposefully slightly simpler than most average content aimed at adults so that it is easier to read or listen to than other titles

Code.CodeDescription: Content adapted or suitable for people with learning / communication difficulties or impairments

This could include content specifically adapted for people with, for example, dyslexia and other reading or learning disabilities, cognitive impairments or disorders, memory disorders, dementia or Alzheimer’s, visual or other sensory impairments, profound and multiple learning disabilities, etc. Use with: 5PM* Qualifiers as appropriate

Code.CodeNotes: Use all 5L* codes for: indicating the content of the work has major themes, topics or storylines relating to or specifically about, or from the perspective of, the main stages of life, or the process of ageing, growing up, the cycle of life from birth to death, or fiction done from the point of view of a person or persons of that stage of life. A novel about teenage anxiety could use 5LF, a romance set amongst students at university could use 5LKE, or a book about Yoga for seniors could use 5LKS. DO NOT USE: to indicate a targeted audience for marketing purposes, the content should be primarily about this stage of life or age group or told from the point of view of that age group

Use for: material that has major or principal themes relating to, or from the perspective of, or primarily about childhood or being a child, or stories told from the point of view of a child

Use for: material that has major or principal themes relating to, or primarily about the years between childhood and adolescence, the passage from being a child to being a teenager, or stories told from the point of view of the preteen or preadolescence

Use for: material that has major or principal themes relating to, or from the perspective of, or primarily about adolescence or being a teenager, the teenage years, the issues, changes, developments that are common for teenagers. Use with: YF* or F* codes when the main themes of a novel are specifically related to the teenage years, being a teenager, specifically from a teenagers point of view, or issues connected with adolescence and use with non-fiction codes for studies, themes or content about teenagers

Use for: material that has major or principal themes relating to, or from the perspective of, or primarily about being an older teenager (roughly 15 to 19 years old), the later teenage years, the issues, changes, developments that are common for older teenagers, also referred to as young adults in some circumstances, post-adolescents. Use with: YF* or F* codes when the main themes of a novel are specifically related to the later teenage years, being an older teenager, specifically from an older teenager’s point of view, or issues connected with late or post adolescence and use with non-fiction codes for studies, themes or content about older teenagers
Use for: material that has major or principal themes relating to, or from the perspective of, or primarily about adulthood or being an adult, life as an adult, etc

Also class here: post-teens, new adult, young adulthood, twenty something, emerging adulthood, etc. Use for: material that is primarily about, or from the perspective of, or has major or principal themes relating to the stage of life spanning from the late teens through to the mid- or late twenties, often centred on topics around becoming an adult or coming of age, progressing from being a teenager to being an adult, those who are newly adult, learning to become an adult. Use with: FR* for ‘New Adult Romance’ or FRG for ‘College Romance’, FP for ‘New Adult Erotica’, FM* for ‘New Adult Fantasy’, etc. when the main themes of a novel are specifically related to this stage of life and use with non-fiction codes for studies, themes or content about this passage from teenager to adult
Use for: material that has major or principal themes relating to, or from the perspective of, or primarily about midlife or middle age

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to migrant groups / diaspora communities or peoples / groups with shared heritage
Code.CodeNotes: Use all 5PBC* codes for: material where the major or principal themes, topics or storylines relating to, or from the perspectives of, or about, (historical and recent) diverse groups of people or persons who have migrated or were exiled or displaced from one part of the world to another; or are part of a diaspora community and who maintain a strong and distinct identity and cultural shared heritage associated with another geographical or cultural area within their present place of residence. Use all 5PBC* codes with: PLACE 1* Qualifiers as appropriate, to indicate the geographical area that is the subject of the work, usually where that group is now, for example, a title about Syrian migrant communities in Sweden, use with 1DNS, or a title about Guatemalan migrant workers in Mexico, use with 1KLCM or a study of German exiled writers of the mid-twentieth century, in the USA, use with 1KBB See also: 5PBD

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to people of the Middle Eastern diasporas / heritage
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: diaspora peoples of Western Asia, Anatolia, the Arabian Peninsula. Use for: material that has major or principal themes, topics or storylines relating to, or from the perspectives of, or about, (historical and recent) Middle Eastern diasporas, or any of the diverse groups or individuals of Middle Eastern heritage living in another geographical area or culture. Use with: PLACE 1* Qualifiers as appropriate, to indicate the scope of the geographical area covered by the group or individual or topic in the work, for example, a biography of an Armenian family in France, use with 1DDF*, or a novel about Turkish migrants in Germany, use with 1DFG*, or a history of Arab Americans in Detroit, use with 1KBB-US-MLGD. Prefer: 1FB* PLACE qualifiers, without 5PBCB, for works about peoples, groups or individuals who live in a particular Middle Eastern country or region, or works about peoples of the Middle East See also: 1FB*

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to specific socioeconomic groups / status
Code.CodeNotes: Use all 5PD* codes for: material that has major or principal themes, topics or storylines relating to, or from the perspective of, or about, social stratification of groups of people or persons based on factors like birth, wealth, income, education, occupation, social status, social or political power, class, etc, or equivalent terminology, and the relative social position within social groups or categories, geographical areas, etc

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to lower socioeconomic groups / status
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: working class, labouring classes, economically disadvantaged, the precariat, etc. Use for: qualifying works that examine or explore the concept of the ‘lower classes’ based on various socioeconomic concepts or that examine aspects of class or status in relation to other subjects, either as a general topic or from a personal point of view, or look at the groups of people or persons who hold the lowest social status, are often the poorest members of a class society, or may wield the least power or influence

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to middle socioeconomic groups / status
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works that examine or explore the concept of the ‘middle classes’ based on various socioeconomic concepts or examine aspects of class or status in relation to other subjects either as a general topic or from a personal point of view, or look at the groups of people or persons who are in the middle of socioeconomic hierarchies

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to higher socioeconomic groups / status
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works that examine or explore the concept of the ‘upper classes’ based on various socioeconomic concepts or examine aspects of class or status in relation to other subjects either as a general topic or from a personal point of view, or look at the groups of people or persons who hold the highest social status, are often the wealthiest members of a class society, or wield the greatest political, economic or social power or influence

Also class here: Royals, Royal families, Kings, Queens, Princesses, Princes, Emperors, Empresses, Aristocrats, Nobility, Nobles, etc. Use for: material that has major or principal themes, topics or storylines relating to, from the perspective of, or about, people, families, dynasties or groups, who have high socioeconomic status based on a usually hereditary title associated with royalty or nobility

Use for: titles featuring scenes or vocabulary, that could cause offence or upset an unaware reader, usually of a sexual or violent or discriminatory nature, and therefore only suitable for a relatively mature teen or an adult audience and where it is considered important that any potential reader is made aware that the content may not be suitable for all. NB: If using 5X with a Y* code it is highly recommended that an explanation of the reason for using it be sent in a descriptive text elsewhere in the titles metadata and that a suitable 5A * Age qualifier be used

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to special / particular aspects of the content
Code.CodeNotes: Use all 5Y* codes for: describing a specific and very particular aspect of the content (not the format) of a title, that is not covered by other qualifiers. DO NOT USE: 5Y itself - always use 5Y* codes

Use for: works that are purposefully written to actively challenge a gender stereotype or norm around gender roles or includes positive representation of non-stereotypical gender roles, e.g. YBC* or YF* codes for children’s stories. NB: Further details of why this qualifier is being used should be sent in other descriptive metadata

Code.CodeDescription: Content relating to body acceptance / body positivity
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works that encourage body acceptance or body neutrality, that show a diverse range of body types, sizes, shapes, that show positive roles for characters, people, or groups of different body types

Code.CodeDescription: Content relates specifically to anthropomorphic characters
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: content that has anthropomorphic characters or uses anthropomorphism as a literary device to tell a story, content that has stories that use the attribution of human traits, emotions, or intentions to non-human entities, such as animals or plants

Code.CodeDescription: Content relates specifically to multiple perspectives
Code.CodeNotes: Also class here: multiperspectivity, polyperspectivity. Use for: content that is shown from more than one perspective, for fiction that uses multiple narrators or a multiple narrative, or for non-fiction where the subject or events are evaluated from multiple different perspectives or points of view

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works where the contents are specifically about or advance some or all of the UN SDG goals or the title is part of a SDG Book Club list

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to UN SDG 1 - Ending Poverty
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works where the contents are specifically about, advance some of the ideas or explore SDG 1 - Ending poverty in all its forms everywhere. (See https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal1)

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to UN SDG 2 - Zero Hunger
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works where the contents are specifically about, advance some of the ideas or explore SDG 2 - End hunger, achieve food security and improved nutrition and promote sustainable agriculture. (See https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal2)

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to UN SDG 3 - Good Health and Well-Being
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works where the contents are specifically about, advance some of the ideas or explore SDG 3 - Ensure healthy lives and promote well-being for all at all ages. (See https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal3)

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to UN SDG 4 - Quality Education
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works where the contents are specifically about, advance some of the ideas or explore SDG 4 - Ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all. (See https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal4)

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to UN SDG 5 - Gender Equality
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works where the contents are specifically about, advance some of the ideas or explore SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls. (See https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal5)

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to UN SDG 6 - Clean Water and Sanitation
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works where the contents are specifically about, advance some of the ideas or explore SDG 6 - Ensure availability and sustainable management of water and sanitation for all. (See https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal6)

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to UN SDG 7 - Affordable and Clean Energy
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works where the contents are specifically about, advance some of the ideas or explore SDG 7 - Ensure access to affordable, reliable, sustainable and modern energy for all. (See https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal7)

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to UN SDG 8 - Decent Work and Economic Growth
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works where the contents are specifically about, advance some of the ideas or explore SDG 8 - Promote sustained, inclusive and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment and decent work for all. (See https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal8)

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to UN SDG 9 - Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works where the contents are specifically about, advance some of the ideas or explore SDG 9 - Build resilient infrastructure, promote inclusive and sustainable industrialization and foster innovation. (See https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal9)

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to UN SDG 10 - Reduced Inequalities
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works where the contents are specifically about, advance some of the ideas or explore SDG 10 - Reduce inequality within and among countries. (See https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal10)

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to UN SDG 11 - Sustainable Cities and Communities
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works where the contents are specifically about, advance some of the ideas or explore SDG 11 - Make cities and human settlements inclusive, safe, resilient and sustainable. (See https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal11)

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to UN SDG 12 - Responsible Consumption and Production
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works where the contents are specifically about, advance some of the ideas or explore SDG 12 - Ensure sustainable consumption and production patterns. (See https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal12)

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to UN SDG 13 - Climate Action
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works where the contents are specifically about, advance some of the ideas or explore SDG 13 - Take urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts. (See https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal13)

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to UN SDG 14 - Life Below Water
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works where the contents are specifically about, advance some of the ideas or explore SDG 14 - Conserve and sustainably use the oceans, seas and marine resources for sustainable development. (See https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal14)

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to UN SDG 15 - Life on Land
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works where the contents are specifically about, advance some of the ideas or explore SDG 15 - Protect, restore and promote sustainable use of terrestrial ecosystems, sustainably manage forests, combat desertification, and halt and reverse land degradation and halt biodiversity loss. (See https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal15)

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to UN SDG 16 - Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works where the contents are specifically about, advance some of the ideas or explore SDG 16 - Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all and build effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels. (See https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal16)

Code.CodeDescription: Relating to UN SDG 17 - Partnerships for Goals
Code.CodeNotes: Use for: works where the contents are specifically about, advance some of the ideas or explore SDG 17 - Strengthen the means of implementation and revitalize the Global Partnership for Sustainable Development. (See https://sdgs.un.org/goals/goal17)
